title: Bittensor Daily News: November 9, 2026
summary: OpenTensor and Injective’s Bangkok Hacker House closes applications November 10. Chutes adds GLM 5.2 Fast, TAO.com announces Arena, and TaoStats reaches its migration deadline. Plus Hippius on iPhone, SOMA’s 11% allocation burn, Score’s vision results, Yanez’s limited BioVault alpha and newly reviewed miner/operator changes.

ecosystem.headline: OpenTensor and Injective set November 10 deadline for Bangkok Hacker House
ecosystem.summary: OpenTensor and Injective reminded builders on November 9 that applications close November 10 for their December 1–10 Bangkok Hacker House. The official program lists accommodation, meals and flight subsidies, with a December 9 demo day. Selected teams may be considered for milestone grants; acceptance and funding are not guaranteed. Applicants must be building on Injective and attend the full program. The published page does not specify the application closing hour or timezone. This is an upcoming builder program, not evidence that participating projects have shipped.
ecosystem.ratingReason: A time-sensitive, primary-confirmed builder opportunity with concrete dates. The event and any resulting products or funding remain future outcomes.

ecosystem.headline: TAO.com announces Arena opening round with a 17.12 TAO prize pool
ecosystem.summary: TAO.com announced Arena on November 9. Its live rules date the opening round from November 6 at 14:30 UTC through November 22 at 23:00 UTC, so the round did not first begin today. The native prize pool is 17.12 TAO, split 50%/30%/20%; the promoted dollar value can change with TAO. Ranking uses eligible realized and unrealized P&L measured in TAO, subject to wallet, trade-size and anti-abuse rules. Entry is advertised as free. No wallet was connected and no entry or trade was made during this review.

sources.label: Live opening-round rules and native prize pool

ecosystem.ratingReason: A concrete product and competition announcement with native rules inspected. Routine competitions are capped at three stars; the prize is denominated in TAO rather than a fixed dollar payout.

ecosystem.headline: TaoStats reaches its November 9 legacy API migration deadline
ecosystem.summary: TaoStats reminded users on November 6 that its legacy API endpoints were due to retire on Monday, November 9. The original October migration guide moves consumers from /api/ routes to /v1/ on the same host and retains existing API keys and authentication. It also documents stricter parameters and pagination changes, including a default of 50 and a maximum of 200 results. This is the previously announced deadline arriving, not a new API launch today. An authenticated legacy-endpoint shutdown check was unavailable, so retirement execution and its exact hour are not independently confirmed.
ecosystem.ratingReason: An actionable deadline for data integrations, supported by the provider’s guide and reminder. Published retirement plans are distinguished from a verified shutdown.

ecosystem.headline: Yuma reports October Large Cap Fund performance
ecosystem.summary: Yuma’s November 9 Large Cap Fund disclosure reports an October return of −16.9% in USD, against −20.9% for its TAO benchmark. That is a 4.0 percentage-point difference while both USD returns were negative. Yuma separately reports +5.0% measured in TAO; that is a different currency basis, not a positive dollar return. These are manager-reported monthly figures and the accompanying chart, not an independently audited NAV or a forecast of future performance.

sources.label: Primary manager disclosure and October chart

ecosystem.ratingReason: A dated manager disclosure worth recording, with currency bases kept separate. No independent NAV reconciliation or new product execution supports a higher rating.

updates.headline: SN4 Targon documents 13.1.0 network persistence and recovery
updates.summary: The November 9 documentation update consolidates 13.1.0 instructions for persistent static networking, bonds and VLAN configuration, including recovery and reboot behavior. This is an operator documentation change, not a newly verified binary release or a production fleet upgrade. Operators should check the applicable version and existing network configuration before applying the documented steps; no installation or network change was performed during this review.
updates.ratingReason: Useful deployment guidance without an independently verified rollout or measured service improvement.

updates.headline: SN28 SayGM announces list-price cuts; exact reduction remains unverified
updates.summary: At 09:00 UTC November 9, SN28 SayGM posted that it is cutting list prices. The current public table labels rates in USD per million tokens and distinguishes recent finalized results from eligible miner offers. During this review, Claude Opus 5.5 displayed $4 input, $0.20 cached input and $20 output per million tokens. Without a directly comparable prior tariff or an effective-time notice, this scan cannot quantify the reduction or say every listed model became cheaper. The six-second attached video is promotional; no complete audio review, paid inference, invoice or provider-performance test was performed.

sources.label: SN28 SayGM current public price units and model table

updates.ratingReason: Useful official pricing notice and dated public tariff snapshot. Missing before/after terms prevent a verified savings percentage or broad commercial-impact claim.

updates.headline: SN28 SayGM changes worker-removal and Phala CVM teardown behavior
updates.summary: SayGM merged an operator change on November 9: gmcli worker remove now deletes the associated Phala CVM by default after successful worker deregistration, with --keep-cvm available to preserve it. The implementation adds preflight checks and distinguishes a successful deregistration followed by failed teardown. A separate merge refreshes compiled Chutes TEE measurement references. Operators should distinguish these merged changes from the later dev-testnet release preparation; a production rollout was not verified. No worker, CVM or account was changed during this review.
updates.ratingReason: A narrowly scoped but consequential operator behavior change, directly reviewed in code. It is not a verified mainnet release or a demonstrated service improvement.

updates.headline: SN31 rec4ll publishes a free tier with explicit memory and processing limits
updates.summary: First directly verified November 8 at 22:22 Eastern, the public product page offered 20 databases,8 million vectors,50 GiB estimated vector storage,1,000 embeddings/hour and 10,000 queries/hour shared by search and generation, without a card or deposit. The page says source text is encrypted at rest but independent operators see plaintext during processing. These published limits are useful for evaluating persistent AI memory, but no API request, reliability test or signup was performed. The original announcement time is unconfirmed. A fresh November 9 page visit returned an empty rendered body, so current availability was not re-established; the published terms are retained as a dated observation.

sources.label: SN31 rec4ll published product and free-tier terms

updates.ratingReason: Concrete published access terms, with a dated observation and current rendering gap. No independent scale, adoption or reliability result supports a higher rating.

updates.headline: SN36 Weir adds seven-day hotkey activation-fee quotes
updates.summary: A November 9 07:55 UTC source change moves GPU activation fees into platform configuration and implements hotkey-bound seven-day quotes. An open quote uses the lower of its quoted fee and the current model fee. Missing configured fees stop new activations while preserving already activated GPUs. Removed hardcoded fee values are not current price quotations. No payment, live quote issuance or deployed fee schedule was tested. At 09:56 Eastern the cached alpha/TAO snapshot showed+15.99% over 24 hours and+2,125.30% over seven days; the latter crosses recent slot reuse and cannot establish a reaction to this commit.
updates.ratingReason: Useful bounded operator change. The rolling price move crosses a registration reset, with limited liquidity, and is not an announcement-aligned causal study or an automatic star increase.

updates.headline: SN44 Score reports three vision skills above their first-week targets
updates.summary: Score published first-week November evaluation figures on November 9: person detection 90.6%, vehicle detection 90.2% and worksite PPE 90.9%, each against a 90% goal. Room dirtiness was 85.8% against 90%, beverage 71.1% against 90%, and cricket delivery 73.0% against 85%. The attached card and post are the team’s own evaluation report. The underlying test sets, metric comparability and live customer outcomes were not independently reproduced; these percentages should not be read as universal real-world accuracy.

sources.label: Primary first-week metrics and evaluation card

updates.ratingReason: A specific six-task progress disclosure with both met and unmet goals retained. Team-reported evaluation figures do not by themselves establish external benchmark superiority or adoption.

updates.headline: SN51 Lium adds GB200 pricing support and changes idle Spot-pay code
updates.summary: November 9 PR2149 adds GB200 as its own GPU family, initially using B200 rental rates and idle caps. Its provider notes require GPU splitting with a minimum of one for idle pay on four-GPU GB200/GB300 trays. Separate merged changes cap idle Spot pay at 80% of the comparable Secure idle rate while retaining the filler-revenue bound, and allow eligible free GPUs on partly rented Spot nodes to receive idle pay without double-paying rented GPUs. Download slowness now requires all measured endpoints to fail the threshold. These are verified code and documentation changes; deployed versions, current payouts, customer savings and installation were not independently tested. Separately, the team’s public statistics page, updated 15:12:37 UTC November 9, displayed $2.6 million billed to renters,1.08 million GPU-hours and28,721 rentals over a rolling 30 days, with 75% utilisation. These are team-reported operational counters, not independently audited revenue or the unverified calendar-October figures. A later November 9 merge distinguishes host GPU loss from other reset failures, provides a compatibility fallback for older backends and lets newer Redis drop records override stale local state. Deployment and a measured reliability improvement were not independently verified.

sources.label: SN51 Lium team-reported public network statistics, November 9 snapshot

updates.ratingReason: Concrete hardware eligibility and payment-formula consequences for operators. No verified live rollout or new revenue record is established.

updates.headline: SN54 Yanez announces limited BioVault password-manager alpha
updates.summary: Late-found November 3 news: Yanez announced a limited BioVault alpha that stores passwords and notes in a browser and requires a fresh face approval in YID to unlock. Access was offered by request rather than as an unrestricted public release. Its version 0.15 guide, updated November 3, says the alpha has not had an independent security review. It documents split browser/server keys and a recovery kit, while warning that losing the required keys or kit can make recovery impossible. Neither the product nor its biometric security was independently tested during this review.

sources.label: Version 0.15 product, encryption and recovery guide

updates.ratingReason: A concrete limited product alpha, supported by the team’s announcement and detailed guide. Limited access, recovery dependencies and the absence of an independent security review constrain the rating.

updates.headline: SN61 RedTeam reports CEO appearance at the House of Lords
updates.summary: RedTeam said on November 9 that its CEO, @oli_innerworks, represented the project at the House of Lords the preceding week, discussing cybersecurity. Its announcement quotes Mark Jeffrey’s November 8 event post. The team’s statement establishes what it is reporting; an official parliamentary record and exact event date were not independently verified in this pass. The appearance is not evidence of a government endorsement, procurement contract or adopted policy.
updates.ratingReason: A primary team-confirmed outreach appearance, with its institutional significance bounded. The rolling token move does not establish a causal response or justify a four-star rating.

updates.headline: SN64 Chutes announces GLM 5.2 Fast support
updates.summary: Chutes announced zai-org/GLM-5.2-Fast on November 9 through its existing OpenAI-compatible endpoint and API keys. Its listing quotes $2.45 per million input tokens and $7.70 per million output tokens. The announcement advertises a one-million-token context and maximum 128K output. The public model catalog independently lists the Fast model; it marks confidential compute false, so this must not be confused with the separate TEE variant. No paid inference, latency test or benchmark reproduction was performed.
updates.ratingReason: A usable model-listing and integration update with a directly checked catalog. Advertised limits are provider claims, and no new adoption or independently measured performance was established.

updates.headline: SN66 Conjectures removes individual chat-log JSON size caps
updates.summary: November 9 PR201 removes per-file JSON byte caps and validates artifact-index entries as a stream. The prior 10 GiB ZIP limit remains, along with 20,000 ZIP entries,64 MiB JSONL line limits,24 levels of JSON nesting and isolated validation resource budgets. Large packages still require multipart upload and adequate scratch storage. This extends the previously covered package-size change; it does not make uploads unlimited or establish that production accepts every package.
updates.ratingReason: Specific submission compatibility change, with the remaining limits retained. No production upload or performance test was performed.

updates.headline: SN71 Leadpoet merges optional weekly Arena reward decay without a floor
updates.summary: November 9 PR1147 adds an optional model-tenure clock: when enabled, occupied slot rewards halve every 140 settlement epochs, approximately seven days, without a four-halving floor. Removed allocation follows the existing burn path rather than going to other holders. Only genuinely new promoted model sources reset the replaced slots; daily documents, restarts and repackaging do not. The switch defaults off in the reviewed service code and requires coordinated validator and gateway activation. Older markerless states retain their previous floor. Follow-up judge recovery and drain guards were also merged. No live activation receipt or executed five-slot eTAO change was verified. Later November 9 merges normalize genesis hashes for reward-clock scope and restore paired restart recovery. A separate attribution change accepts reversed legal-name/initialism labels only alongside verified company bindings and refreshes deferred industry guidance. These are code changes, not verified production payouts.

sources.label: Later primary reward-clock and restart merge

updates.ratingReason: Material proposed incentive behavior supported by merged code, with default-off activation explicitly preserved. Not evidence of an executed transaction burn or active allocation change.

updates.headline: SN75 Hippius confirms iPhone availability, following its earlier Android release
updates.summary: At 08:57 UTC November 9, SN75 Hippius announced mobile availability. The official download page links to working Apple and Google Play listings from T34 Corporation. Apple’s public metadata dates the iPhone release to November 6, with version 1.2.0 updated at 14:56:56 UTC that day and iOS 15.1 required; this is a late-found release, not a claim it first shipped today. Android availability was already covered September 21 and is not a second launch. The product and store pages describe automatic photo/video backup and access to desktop files, with encryption before upload. Listings and announcement media were checked, but no app was installed, backup performed or encryption implementation independently audited. Availability does not establish downloads, paid adoption or customer revenue.

updates.headline: SN97 Ingot tightens challenger KL margin and revises evaluation weighting
updates.summary: Ingot merged a November 9 evaluation change reducing the challenger KL margin from 3% to 2% relative to the incumbent’s own KL. Within each domain, KL is now weighted across answer tokens before domains are combined by their sample shares, replacing the earlier mean of per-sample normalized values. The 800-sample mix shifts terminal tasks from 300 to 330 and math from 50 to 20, alongside a dataset revision. Dashboard rescoring is intended to make older duels comparable. This is reviewed merged code, not independently verified production activation, model superiority or changed payouts.
updates.ratingReason: A substantive, inspectable change to miner evaluation and the challenger threshold. Production activation and economic effects remain unverified, preventing an upgrade based solely on the merge.

The progress panel describes 320 papers and 30 pipelines, which is a different counter from accepted packages. No winner, completed evaluation or reward distribution is established. The following weekly intake remains a separate round. This updates the earlier overnight submissions-open and queued states rather than announcing another competition.

updates.headline: SN114 SOMA sets an 11% emission burn allocation
updates.summary: At 12:18:12 UTC November 9, finalized block 9,468,579, extrinsic 8, event 171 executes a successful proxied allocation change. The full vector moves from 0% burn /0% recycle /about 18% owner /about 41% validators /about 41% miners to 11% burn /0% recycle /about 18% owner /30% validators /about 41% miners. Exact integer vectors and before/after storage are preserved in the evidence; small normalization differences are rounded here. SOMA’s registration, identity and owner remain unchanged. This configures the division of future alpha emissions, not a separately executed transaction burn. Root’s live baseline is paid from and capped by the validator bucket; alpha validators share the remainder, and historical yield can lag the change.

sources.label: Finalized SN114 SOMA vectors and successful proxy execution

updates.ratingReason: Executed material reward-direction change, with full event/storage proof. No guaranteed yield, price outcome or already-destroyed token amount is inferred.

updates.headline: SN117 EveryFrame publishes everycli 1.0.0 and separate worker-upgrade requirements
updates.summary: The November 9 13:39 UTC merge publishes version 1.0.0, redesigned miner health checks and job diagnostics. Its release notes describe optional price-based offers, provider routes for additional models and updated Phala provisioning. Automatic offers default off and pause when complete current prices are unavailable. CLI updating alone does not update the deployed worker or enable offers; the notes require a compatible signed worker for the new capabilities and review of Miner Terms. Existing manual offers are preserved. These are released source and documented requirements, not an independently installed client, verified provider availability or demonstrated miner profit.
updates.ratingReason: Useful operator release with explicit upgrade and activation boundaries. No independently measured production scale or performance breakthrough.

updates.headline: SN127 Zils merges customer training-data cleanup around jobs
updates.summary: November 9 PR222 adds cleanup of customer training rows, photos and partial downloads before claim and after job completion; finite round fleets remove their last-round rows. A completed frozen candidate can still be delivered after its training rows are removed. This does not erase candidate artifacts, raw outputs or logs. Seven-day archive cleanup and stopping an unbounded fleet remain manual responsibilities. The change follows the previously covered delivery gates; it is verified implementation, not independent proof that every deployed miner erased its data. Later on November 9, PR223 adds an incumbent-ensemble guard: a new greedy combination must improve on the current ensemble by at least 0.5 score points on the same decision items before replacing it. The guard does not preserve an ensemble that cannot be rebuilt because a member is unknown or was not graded this round; identical membership needs no extra comparison. The merged implementation does not establish production rollout, an actual missed payment or a repaired round. A later November 9 merge also reports the miner’s installed commit during job claims and surfaces coordinator upgrade refusals. The documented admission window requires matching coordinator support; the merge alone does not prove fleet-wide activation.

updates.ratingReason: Concrete training-data lifecycle and model-selection safeguards, with retained artifacts, manual responsibilities and current-ensemble eligibility disclosed. No blanket erasure guarantee or production payout repair is inferred.
